reason: A count of flowers in the word (suffix 'flowered' -> flower in config/flora_counted_parts.tsv) with the vague number 'few'. That count is held as measurement_value_not_numeric, as the count pattern says; 'few' alone was rejected as a bearer before.
A hyphenated compound of two shapes is a continuum between ovate (FLOPO:0991024, 2-D) and lanceolate (PATO_0001877), as for 'linear-lanceolate'.
FLOPO stipitate is 'borne on a stalk or stipe' and already has 'stalked' as a synonym. This covers ovaries, paraphyses, bulbils and glands; leaves stay with petiolate where a parser maps them.

target: new: wall of the bearer (part of the bearer, slot 1) + decreased thickness (PATO_0000592)
reason: What is thin is the wall, not the cell or fruit: bearer substituted by the wall (pericarp PO_0009084, plant ovary wall PO_0005022, sporangium wall PO_0025306; the cell wall is GO, not PO) with decreased thickness. Mostly bryophyte leaf cells, which need the cell-wall bearer decided first.

target: new: wall of the bearer (part of the bearer, slot 1) + increased thickness (PATO_0000591)
reason: Same as thin-walled: the quality is the thickness of the wall of the cell, fruit or stem. It needs the wall as the substituted bearer, not a new term.

'Veins visible' means clearly visible, as with the earlier rules for evident and obvious (C323, C324). 'Hardly visible' is a degree modifier on the same value; the surface ('adaxially') goes in the part-of-bearer slot.

Divergent stigmas, wings, lobes and branches are directed outward, away from one another and the axis, which is PATO spreading's definition. FLOPO:0991080 divaricate is the stronger 'widely spreading', and PATO_0002424 divergent from is relational.
Eglandular = without glands. Gland is the bearer rule C265 (PO_0005656), and the absence follows ebracteate and awnless; 'hairs eglandular' says the same of the hairs.
Unarmed = without spines, thorns or prickles, the negation of 'armed', which PATO spiny covers ('spines, thorns or similar thin projections'); same form as unlobed.

Most uses are 'veins/nervis parallel', i.e. parallel venation, as the earlier rule for parallel-veined (C341). Parallel fibres, wings or anthers need the thing they are parallel to (PATO_0002272 parallel to is relational) and stay unresolved.
A naked stem or scape is leafless. A naked receptacle (no paleae), antheridium (no paraphyses) or sinus (no vein border) lacks a different part each time and is left to the context.
FLOPO caespitose has 'tufted' as a synonym for plants and stems in dense clumps. 'Tufts of hairs' is bearded/comose, and tufted basal leaves are a leaf cluster, so both stay outside this rule.
A once-ternate leaf has three leaflets. '1-2-ternate' and 'biternate' are further divisions and need their own reading (like bipinnate), and 'spikelets ternate' (in threes) is a count of parts.
The approximate-value pattern names 'suborbicular' as its example: orbicular (PATO_0001934) with value_qualifier 'sub', the whole word as cue.
Not a continuum: the apex narrows (acuminate) into a tail, and both hold. Caudate, 'having a tail or tail-like projection', says the more specific part.
Acutish = somewhat acute, a point less sharp than acute but not rounded, which is FLOPO subacute's definition.
PATO circular has 'round' and 'rounded' as related synonyms (round seeds, disks, sori, apices). 'Petiole round' in cross-section means terete and is better read in the context of a section.

label: monomorphic
definition: A morphological quality inhering in a set of homologous plant structures by virtue of its members occurring in a single form. NOTE: Sibling and opposite of FLOPO:0991092 dimorphic; 'not dimorphic' would also cover trimorphic sets.
reason: Stated of leaves, tepals, achenes and stolons in many floras. It is the positive opposite of FLOPO dimorphic, which a negation cannot replace.

A compound leaf is a PO class, not a quality. A named compound inflorescence has its PO class (compound raceme PO_0030116, spike PO_0030118, capitulum PO_0030122, umbel PO_0030130); a bare 'inflorescence compound' is branched (PATO_0000402).

A double peristome or pappus is in two rows. 'Costa double' is a count of two, 'flowers double' is a garden form with extra petals, and 'margin double' is a fragment of doubly serrate, so all three stay unresolved.

label: wiry
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being slender, tough and resilient, like wire. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991126 corky; combines slenderness with toughness, which PATO:0001545 inflexible does not.
reason: A frequent, well-defined description of stems, culms, pedicels and scapes, with no PATO or FLOPO term.
'Bi-dentate' = two teeth; 'dentate' is a counted suffix (tooth) in config/flora_counted_parts.tsv, so it is a count of 2 teeth, at the apex where stated.
A petiole sheathed at the base forms a sheath round the axis (FLOPO sheathing). 'Capsule sheathed in the perichaetial leaves' is enclosed by another part and needs the relation pattern 09.
A gland at the tip of the tooth, anther or hair: the gland's presence, put at the apex region by the part-of-bearer slot. Gland-tipped hairs on an organ are FLOPO:0991173 glandular-pubescent.
A degree of development with no fixed meaning apart from the organ. Where it only says the part is there, the part's own mention states its presence.
'Marked' needs what the part is marked with (spots, lines, leaf scars); that marking is the quality, as with 'covered' (C240).
Broadened bases and apices are widened, as in the rule for 'widened' (C182). The region (base, apex) goes in the part-of-bearer slot.
Armed = bearing spines, thorns or prickles, which PATO spiny defines. The kind of armature, when named, is a part (thorn PO_0025172, prickle PO_0025169).
Glandless = without glands ('Glands: Absent'). It is the absence of the gland bearer C265, the same rule as eglandular.

target: new: two values of one bearer (ovate FLOPO:0991024 and asymmetrical PATO_0000616)
reason: Not a continuum: the outline is ovate and the base or sides are unequal (oblique = inequilateral, rule C236), so both values hold together.
